correctness.rationale: The cited WHB duality sends an expansion of the fixed product ∏C_(n_i+1) to independent monotone Ferrers blocks on disjoint dual chains. Nonzero block endpoints u,v have exactly binom(u+v−2,u−1) interior threshold fillings. The active graph within one block is connected through the first source and final target point, even in diagonal blocks; the overlap graph H of endpoint supports therefore gives its union-components. Remaining uncovered dual vertices number Σ_i max(0,n_i−U_i−V_i), proving Boolean congruence rank I+κ(H) via Theorem 5.10. Direct independent enumeration of all relations on (1,1) gives {1:12,2:4} and on (2,2) gives {1:1213,2:70,3:12,4:1}; these agree with the formula but are not proof for all vectors. For uniformly random s×t Ferrers blocks, the binomial ratio for at least half zero rows is at most exp[−min(s,t)/4]; similarly for target columns. Union bound over both tails in k² blocks ensures overlapping longer-than-half prefixes and suffixes, no isolates, and connected H, hence simplicity probability ≥1−2k² exp(−m/4). Boundary k≥2,n_i≥1, named operations and fixed-k complexity are respected.
residual_risks: General WHB duality and congruence correspondence are cited mathematical inputs not re-proved. The probability inequality is a sufficient-event lower bound, not an exact probability or sharp asymptotic.

The 2015 algorithm counts one-connective weak Heyting algebras up to isomorphism, rather than the paired WHB operations with their congruence-profile distribution; full-text comparison remains inaccessible.

value.rationale: Simplicity and full congruence-rank spectra are intrinsic algebraic invariants for subdirect decomposition. A compact exact endpoint-weight generating function replaces an enormous enumeration of operations for any fixed factor count and yields quantitative generic simplicity across a natural infinite class of distributive lattice reducts; these are mathematically motivated objects, not arbitrary tiny tables.
residual_risks: Fixed-k polynomial-time exponent grows quickly with k; the result does not enumerate isomorphism types and its generic bound is not optimal.

limitations: Named paired WHB expansions only; k≥2 and n_i≥1, fixed-k polynomial-time qualification.
Relies on 2023 WHB duality, finite experiments limited to small dual posets.
